text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The European Commission in Brussels is today due to release a preliminary verdict on which countries actually fulfill the Maastricht Treaty's requirements to join European Monetary Union. Italy is seen underperforming other EU countries and missing the EMU target (all).
* President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro, on a visit to Berlin, said the country's political uncertainties would be overcome and Italy would qualify for EMU (all).
* An Italian navy ship in a multinational security mission to Albania ran aground in stormy seas off the coast of the rebel-held city of Vlore (all).
* Transport unions launched the first in a wave of strikes that look set to hamper travel in Italy over the next two weeks (all).

* April consumer price index as shown by preliminary data from a further five sample cities indicated inflation falling to 0.1 month-on-month and 1.7 percent year-on-year. Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said he was confident CPI would remain subdued, raising hopes for an interest rate cut (all).
* Giorgio Fossa, head of Italian employers' federation Confindustria, said the association would defend a labour agreement even if it meant forcing the government to call a confidence vote (all).

* Agro-industry and chemical group Montedison reported 1996 consolidated net profit of 298 billion lire, with 1996 operating profits rising some 3.7 percent to 1.982 trillion lire. The group's consolidated net debt fell 15.4 percent to 8.324 trillion lire. At the parent company level, 1996 net profits rose 30.4 percent to 330 billion lire 1996, while it will pay an ordinary share dividend of 20 lire a share and 150 lire a share for savings shares (La Repubblica).

* Insurance company RAS said it saw its 1996 parent net profit rise 6.1 percent to 338 billion lire in 1995, but it left its 1996 ordinary share dividend unchanged at 340 lire. The group added that it had increased its stake in Italian banking group Credito Italiano to five percent, and that it had also held its 1996 dividend on its savings shares at 400 lire per share (all).
* French bank Credit Lyonnais said it would put up for sale in the next few days its 56.8 percent stake in Italy's Credito Bergamasco (all).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
